findings.location: Results, Delphi-item ratings p.4 vs results/final/0.main_table.csv
findings.evidence: Text: 'the median percentage of participants that rated an item as essential was 74% (interquartile range = 60%-86%). The median of the average (mean) rating across the 78 items was 7.4 (interquartile range = 6.8-7.9)'. Stored main_table (72 non-NA items): median 70.0% (IQR 54.25-85.0), median mean 7.21 (IQR 6.66-7.92). My recount from data/1.item_ratings.csv: 70.1% (55.0-85.15) and 7.21 (6.68-7.90). [Red (build_passport.py, archive_verified): the verification stage printed the authors' stored value with an executed check and upheld the conflict.]
findings.question_for_authors: Which sample and item set produced the reported 74% and 7.4 medians?

findings.location: Results, Delphi-item ratings p.4 vs materials/results/final/0.main_table.csv (72 non-NA items, median of mean)
findings.evidence: The paper reports 'median of mean ratings' = 7.4 scale 1-9 (Results, Delphi-item ratings p.4); the authors' own stored output (materials/results/final/0.main_table.csv (72 non-NA items, median of mean)) gives 7.21. Our re-run gives 7.21, which matches the stored output. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run. Yellow, not red: 0.main_table.csv holds the columns mean, mean.1. The paper's table may be built from another version of the column; add `archive_code` (file:line of the authors' code that writes the paper's number) to recomputed.json once that column is confirmed.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'median of mean ratings' (7.4), given that materials/results/final/0.main_table.csv (72 non-NA items, median of mean) gives 7.21?

findings.evidence: The paper defines a threshold of at least 70% ("### Definition of consensus Before launching the survey, the steering committee defined consensus as at least 70% of participants in each nonstudent stakeholder group rating an item as “essential” (i.e., between 7 and 9 "), but no comparison in the code uses 0.7; the code compares at 0.75 (`consensus = if_else(perc_essential >= 0.75, TRUE, FALSE),`). Check which threshold produced the reported results.
